items.title: 67247_J.C. Higginbotham oral history interview
items.q: We lived in the same building in the same street as Fletcher Henderson, Pinky Bujimi.

ctx.x: Who was leading - who started inciting all these people to think like this? Was it anybody in particular or everybody just felt that way?

I mentioned one but you don't know him. He's a drummer, very good drummer, name was Pinky ( ? ). That's when Local 802 was on Lexington Avenue because I went over there to join. They was fighting about who wanted to be who or whom. Fighting about the president and the secretary and he was fighting the president. We lived in the same building in the same street as Fletcher Henderson, Pinky Bujimi. He's a Negro drummer and a very good one too and would fight anybody anytime. He'd say, we're entitled to it just as…
What was the white argument. What did they say?
